title: How Buildings Learn
creator: Stewart Brand
why_it_matters: It makes continuity legible as adaptation over time rather than purity at a single moment. That matters for machine-room tools, which are being asked to remain themselves while changing through use.
why_now: Even paused, it still exerts pressure because the foundry is negotiating reuse, revision, and growth. The project line is not to freeze a system in place but to let it learn without losing shape.
active_questions: How does a local tool change through use without becoming a different kind of thing?
What should remain stable, and what should stay easy to revise by hand?
signals: Use leaves traces; a good system should expect them.
Durability often comes from layered change rather than polished stasis.

return_markers.why_now: The distinction between rigid consistency and layered continuity needed a better supporting source.

notes: Status is paused, but pressure remains high because it keeps feeding continuity language.
Good proof that active pressure should not equal open-tab recency.
